_doc: F3f vocabulary-floor expansions, per tab. Key = a distinctive term of art occurring in that tab's MUST feature text; value = a GENUS restatement inserted IN PLACE right after the match, so every structural element of the feature survives. Adopted forward-only 2026-08-29 (user). t10's map is the one validated by the clean A/B ab_clean_t10_1787900564.json; t12/t13/t14 written from each tab's own MUST list. Keys must not nest inside one another.

10.wireless power supply: wireless/contactless power transfer of any kind — microwave, RF, inductive, magnetic-resonance or capacitive power feeding, including 'power transmission', 'energy harvesting from a transmitted field', 'RF-to-DC rectenna supply' and equivalents
10.microwave: microwave or radio-frequency carrier used to carry power (any band described as RF, UHF, SHF, ISM, 2.4 GHz, 5.8 GHz, 900 MHz or 'radio waves')
10.wireless communication link: any bidirectional or unidirectional radio data link between the two named units — BLE, Zigbee, Wi-Fi, LoRa, NFC, proprietary sub-GHz, 'radio telemetry', 'wireless signal transmission'
10.stroke position: position/displacement/travel/extension of a moving member (piston, rod, spool, plunger, slide, actuator shaft), whether reported as absolute position, stroke length, displacement or travel
10.magnetic sensor: any magnetically-sensing element — Hall element, magnetoresistive (AMR/GMR/TMR), reed, fluxgate, magnetostrictive or inductive position sensor

12.first fan: any air-moving element — fan, blower, impeller, ventilator, axial or centrifugal fan, air circulator or forced-convection air mover
12.water-cooled power supply: a power supply, converter, rectifier or power unit cooled by a circulating liquid coolant — water, deionized water, water-glycol, a cooling jacket, a cold plate or a liquid-cooled heat sink
12.chiller: any refrigeration or heat-rejection unit — chiller, refrigeration machine, heat exchanger, cooling tower, radiator-and-pump loop, or thermostatic coolant circulator
12.charging and discharging jig: any fixture, tray, rack, probe block or contact assembly that connects battery cells for charge/discharge cycling — formation jig, cycler contact block, test fixture, probe tray
12.water-supply pipe: any coolant supply line — inlet pipe, hose, conduit, feed line or supply manifold
12.drainpipe: any coolant return line — outlet pipe, return hose, discharge conduit or return manifold
12.charger and discharger: battery formation or cycling equipment of any name — charge/discharge tester, cycler, formation system, battery test station

13.wireless communication module: any radio transceiver module — Wi-Fi, Bluetooth/BLE, Zigbee, 5G/NB-IoT/LTE-M, LoRa, sub-GHz proprietary RF, NFC or an RF SoC performing the same role
13.control module: any controller, MCU, microcontroller, processor board, logic unit, ECU or embedded control circuit performing the control role
13.wired communication interface: any wired bus or port — CAN or CAN-FD, LIN, RS-485/RS-232, UART, I2C, SPI, Ethernet, single-wire serial, or a wiring-harness connector carrying the same signals
13.battery management equipment: a BMS, battery management system, battery controller, pack monitoring unit or battery ECU
13.target battery device: the battery pack, module, cell assembly or energy-storage unit being woken, activated, enabled or started
13.message generating device: any unit that composes, encodes or assembles a command frame, data telegram or bus message
13.input device: any terminal supplying the data — smartphone, tablet, PC, handheld programmer, HMI panel, or a web/app client
13.transceiver: any bus driver, line driver or PHY converting logic-level signals to bus levels and back
13.target message: the command, parameter set or payload conveyed, under any name — frame, telegram, packet, instruction or data record

14.charge state graph: any curve, plot, profile, table, array or time series of state of charge (SOC) against time or against charged capacity, however represented
14.voltage pattern graph: any voltage-against-time or voltage-against-capacity curve — charge voltage profile, V-Q curve, dV/dQ or dV/dt curve, or a tabulated equivalent
14.inflection angle: any quantified measure of the bend or knee at the transition point — an angle, a slope difference, a curvature value, a dV/dt or dV/dQ step, or a knee-point metric
14.inflection occurs: a knee, bend, break point, transition, slope discontinuity or curvature change appears
14.state change rate: any degradation, aging or health metric expressed as a ratio or percentage against an initial or reference state — SOH, capacity-fade ratio, degradation coefficient, deterioration rate
14.charge current threshold: a cut-off or termination current, taper current, or end-of-charge current criterion
14.charge voltage upper limit: a maximum or ceiling charge voltage, cut-off voltage or upper voltage limit
14.hyperbolic tangent: tanh, or any sigmoid / S-shaped saturating function
14.charge mode: a charging stage, phase or step (CC stage, CV stage, taper stage)
14.charging device: a charger, charging circuit, power supply or on-board/off-board charging unit
14.computer-readable medium: a non-transitory storage medium, memory, firmware image or computer program product
